group_note: All six are single-question biology items with four short text options and no printed statement block, list or figure, so the packet's grouping on structure `plain` holds for every member and no member had to be set aside. The demand axis was decided by one test applied to all six: does one stored fact name the answer without the options having to be weighed against each other? It does in all six, so all six are `recall` and none is `concept_discrimination` - the rulebook's `concept_discrimination` excludes "recalling one", and in q107 and q106 the stored definition (codominance; sporogenesis is meiotic) names its option directly even though the distractors are neighbouring definitions. That the distractors are neighbouring concepts is recorded where it belongs, as `neighbouring_fact` on the trap axis, not as a second kind of thinking. Solution structure follows a second single test: `several_independent_checks` only where the task forces a separate verdict on each option or on each of two named subjects - q104, whose negated task "did not use" sends every option back to the list of seven characters, and q106, whose option must hold for both microsporogenesis and megasporogenesis. The other four are `single_step`, since one stored fact names the option and the rest need no adjudication. Elimination was recorded only where one named fact strikes out named options and that fact is cheaper than the answer itself: the cell-layer names in q103, the three Mendelian characters in q104, the two-site conjunction in q106. It was withheld from q105, q107 and q108, where the only available shortcut is already knowing the answer. On the trap axis the recurring device across the group is an option carrying a true fact about a neighbour - another follicular layer (q103), the adjacent process gametogenesis (q106), complete dominance and linkage (q107), vertebrate matrix glycosaminoglycans (q108) - and it is labelled by what kind of neighbour it is, following the rulebook's tie-break: `other_one_fact` where a different member of the same family is named (the granulosa, in the same follicle as the key), `neighbouring_fact` where the families themselves differ (linkage, gametogenesis, cartilage matrix). q104 is the only member whose task is negated, and it is also the only one carrying `true_statement_trap`, three times, which is the correct consequence of that polarity rather than a difference in judgement. Four options across the group were deliberately left untagged (q103 option 3, q105 option 2, q108 option 1, and no second entry on any answer option) because no option-and-route pair could be named for them, which rule 4 requires. No trap is placed on any official answer, and no `new_*` escape was needed in this packet.
